why_this_matters: Day 161 sits in Phase 9 (Excel + Power BI + Tableau), whose goal is: Be dangerous in the BI stack that most employers actually use. Today's core material - Tableau Public install and interface, Dimensions vs measures, Discrete vs continuous (green vs blue) - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

concept.what: Tableau Fundamentals - a guided source lesson. The topic list below is the exact scope covered by the original recordings and repository notebooks linked in this lesson.
concept.why: Because every downstream day assumes this vocabulary. Skipping it creates silent gaps that surface later as 'my model does not work and I do not know why'.
concept.how: Work through the topic cards in order: read the linked source moment, run the linked repository code, then answer the reflection prompts in your own words before moving on.
concept.intuition: Treat each topic as a question the instructor was answering. Find the question, then the answer becomes memorable.
concept.analogy: Building this phase is like learning to drive: watching is not enough, and neither is memorising the manual. You need wheel time on real datasets.
concept.internals: Use the linked notebooks to see real implementations, then step one level deeper: for each library call, ask what data structure and loops it replaces.
concept.visual: Sketch the pipeline of today's topic yourself: inputs -> processing -> outputs. The diagram section contains a generated structure you can copy.
concept.deep: Advanced learners: implement the smallest possible version of today's topic from scratch (no library) before using the library version.
concept.math: Identify which quantity in today's topic is being summed, averaged, or maximised. That quantity is the maths to understand first.

code.heading: 10. Tree Map
code.code:
# Import required libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import squarify # install if you do not have it

# Sample data
data = {
    'File Type': ['Documents', 'Videos', 'Images', 'Audio', 'Other'],
    'Storage Used (GB)': [50, 150, 80, 60, 10]
}

# Create a pandas dataframe from the dictionary
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Plotting the treemap
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
colors = ['red', 'green', 'blue', 'yellow', 'grey']
squarify.plot(sizes=df['Storage Used (GB)'], label=df['File Type'], color=colors, alpha=0.6)

# Add title
plt.title('Storage Used by File Type')
plt.axis('off')  # Turn off the axis

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('./outputs/plots/treemap.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Display the plot
plt.show()

code.heading: Make predictions
code.code:
# draw a confusion matrix
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix

# Assuming you have already trained your model and obtained the predicted labels and true labels
# predicted_labels and true_labels are NumPy arrays containing the predicted and true labels respectively

# Convert continuous predictions to discrete class labels
predicted_labels = np.argmax(predictions, axis=1)
# Create the confusion matrix
cm = confusion_matrix(test_labels, predicted_labels)

# Define the class labels for Fashion MNIST (assuming there are 10 classes)
class_labels = ['T-shirt/top', 'Trouser', 'Pullover', 'Dress', 'Coat', 'Sandal', 'Shirt', 'Sneaker', 'Bag', 'Ankle boot']

# Plot the confusion matrix
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.imshow(cm, interpolation='nearest', cmap=plt.cm.Blues)
plt.title('Confusion Matrix for Fashion MNIST')
plt.colorbar()
tick_marks = np.arange(len(class_labels))
plt.xticks(tick_marks, class_labels, rotation=45)
plt.yticks(tick_marks, class_labels)
plt.xlabel('Predicted Label')
plt.ylabel('True Label')

# Add values to the confusion matrix plot
thresh = cm.max() / 2.
for i in range(cm.shape[0]):
    for j in range(cm.shape[1]):
        plt.text(j, i, format(cm[i, j], 'd'),
                 horizontalalignment="center",
                 color="white" if cm[i, j] > thresh else "black")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Tableau Public install and interface on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).

interview_questions.q: What is Tableau Public install and interface, and where would you use it in a real project?
interview_questions.a: Answer using: definition -> why it exists -> one concrete project example -> one limitation. The limitation is what separates senior answers.

interview_questions.q: Describe a bug you would expect when misusing Loading and shaping data.
interview_questions.a: Name the symptom, the underlying cause, and the check you would run to confirm it.

real_world: Roles that use Tableau Public install and interface daily: data analyst, data scientist and ML engineer. In industry the tool matters less than the judgement about when to use it - that judgement is what interviews and performance reviews reward.
production: Version the inputs and the code, not just the output.
Make the step rerunnable: a script you are afraid to re-run is a liability.
Log what happened (counts in, counts out) so failures are detectable.
